artists.biography: Elizabeth Caroline Orton is an English musician. Known for her "folktronica" sound, which mixes elements of folk and electronica, she was initially recognised for her collaborations with William Orbit, Andrew Weatherall, Red Snapper and the Chemical Brothers in the mid-1990s. Her UK/US first solo album, Trailer Park, received much critical acclaim in 1996. Orton developed a devoted audience with the release of the BRIT Award-winning album Central Reservation (1999) and the 2002 UK top 10 album, Daybreaker. Her 2006 album, Comfort of Strangers, was followed by a break during which Orton gave birth to her daughter and collaborated with the British guitarist Bert Jansch. Orton returned with Sugaring Season in 2012, which moved towards a purer acoustic sound, followed by a return to electronic music with Kidsticks, released in 2016.

editorialNotes.short: An ornate, deeply moving ninth album that finds Orton in raw, powerful form.

raw_attributes.name: The Ground Above

perplexity.description:
Beth Orton’s ninth album, The Ground Above, released on June 26, 2026 via Partisan Records, marks her most direct and unapologetic musical statement to date. Urgent, raw, embodied, and emotionally fearless, the album moves between subconscious expression and expansive, timeless songcraft, serving as a testament to Orton’s enduring artistry. Self-produced by Orton following the same collective spirit as her 2022 breakthrough Weather Alive, the record was sculpted over a year-long process from initial live recordings, trusting slowness as its songs hover, circle, and release. The album explicitly explores themes of survival, renewal, motherhood, identity, political unease, and the ongoing choice to stay in love, art, and the world.

Musically, The Ground Above features Orton’s voice ranging from whispered incantation to primal wail, delivering melodies reminiscent of classic songbook forms while collaborating with trusted musicians like multi-instrumentalist Shahzad Ismaily, drummers Chris Vatalaro and Vishal Nayak, and bassist Tom Herbert. The eight-track collection, including titles such as “Before I Knew,” “Cigarette Curls,” and “Celestial Light,” trusts in the openness of difficult feelings, leaving the way forward unobstructed. As Orton’s antenna to the cosmos for over 30 years, this album reaffirms her role as the poet laureate of forces too vast to grasp all at once, reaching new heights as both a producer and songwriter.
